recognize_zh: 多格組圖呈現 POEMS 症候群的臨床面向：腹部 CT 腹水與器官腫大、胸部 X 光橫膈抬高且肺功能隨治療改善、PET/CT 骨頭硬化性病灶、足部紅紫色變化、軀幹多發血管瘤（箭頭）以及外觀多血、腹部膨大，而非單一細胞形態學。
features: A: axial abdominal CT with ascites and enlarged abdominal organs
B-C: chest radiographs with reduced lung volumes and elevated hemidiaphragms (2002) improving by 2005, paralleled by improved TLC, PImax, FEV1 and DLCO
D-E: FDG-PET/CT and CT showing a focal osseous lesion in the right shoulder girdle region, consistent with a sclerotic plasmacytoma
F: violaceous discoloration of the feet and toes (acrocyanosis)
G-H: multiple small red-purple papules on the trunk (arrows) consistent with hemangiomas, followed over time
I: plethora, skin hyperpigmentation and abdominal distension; non-morphologic clinical/radiologic composite
describe_en: Composite clinical and radiologic figure illustrating POEMS syndrome rather than a cytologic specimen. Abdominal CT (A) shows ascites with organomegaly, and serial chest radiographs (B, C) show restrictive physiology with elevated hemidiaphragms and low lung volumes that improve over time, as documented by the accompanying pulmonary function values. PET/CT and CT (D, E) demonstrate a focal FDG-avid bone lesion in the shoulder girdle consistent with a sclerotic bone lesion/plasmacytoma. Clinical photographs show acrocyanosis of the feet (F), multiple truncal hemangiomas (G, H, arrows), and plethora, hyperpigmentation and abdominal distension (I). Together these features illustrate the extravascular volume overload, sclerotic bone lesions and skin changes characteristic of POEMS syndrome, which requires polyneuropathy and a monoclonal (usually lambda) plasma cell disorder for diagnosis.

ddx.vs: Myeloma causes lytic lesions, anemia, hypercalcemia and renal failure with heavy marrow plasmacytosis, whereas POEMS has sclerotic lesions, low marrow plasma cell burden, polyneuropathy and high VEGF.
AL amyloidosis causes neuropathy and organomegaly but lacks sclerotic bone lesions, hemangiomas and polycythemia, and tissue biopsy is Congo red-positive.
Castleman disease shares effusions and lymphadenopathy and can coexist with POEMS, but without polyneuropathy and a clonal plasma cell disorder it does not meet POEMS criteria.

captions: A: CT abdomen with ascites and organomegaly; B-C: chest radiographs with improving pulmonary function; D-E: PET/CT and CT of sclerotic bone lesion; F: acrocyanosis of feet; G-H: truncal hemangiomas (arrows); I: plethora, hyperpigmentation and abdominal distension
